description: CONVERSION OF C3 DWELLINGHOUSE TO X2 C3 UNITS (X1 5B7P & X1 1B1P). IN ORDER TO FACILITATE THE CONVERSION THE FOLLOWING ADDITIONS ARE PROPOSED: ERECTION OF PART SINGLE/PART TWO STOREY REAR EXTENSION; REAR DORMER; INSERTION OF ROOF ABOVE THE TWO STOREY SIDE ADDITION; INSERTION OF A TERRACE AT FIRST FLOOR AND CONVERSION OF GARAGE INTO HABITABLE ROOM
decision_conditions: Reason : 1 - The proposed development would result in a poor standard of accommodation to the detriment of the amenities of future occupiers due to inadequate internal spaces. Both units would fail to provide an acceptable standard of residential accommodation and living space resulting in unsatisfactory standard of accommodation to the detriment of the amenities of future occupiers. The proposals would therefore be contrary to policy D6 of the London Plan and Merton Local Plan policies D12.1, D12.3 and D12.4

Reason : 2 - The proposed roof above the existing two storey addition, rear dormer, first floor rear terrace and first floor rear addition, by reason of design, size, scale, bulk, mass, detailing and materials, would result in an unsympathetic and incongruous form of overdevelopment that fails to achieve a high standard of design to the detriment of the character and appearance of the host property, the terrace row it forms a part of and visual amenity of the locality, contrary to policies D3 (Optimising site capacity through the design-led approach) & D4 (Delivering good design) of the London Plan 2021 & Merton Local Plan policies D12.1, D12.3 and D12.4

Reason : 3 - The proposed first floor addition and roof terrace, including the screening, by reason of its combined siting, design, depth, height, scale and form results in an overbearing, prominent, dominant, visually intrusive and unneighbourly form of development that fails to safeguard residential amenity of nearby occupants in terms of loss of privacy, overlooking and create sense of enclosure, in particular to 53 & 57 Stanford Way.  Its elevated position offering opportunity for prolonged stay has the potential to cause of noise disturbance to the occupiers of 57 Stanford Way in particular.  The scheme is contrary to, in particular, planning policy D12.3 of Merton's Local Plan 2025 and policies D3 , D4  & D14 of the London Plan (2021)

Reason : 4 - The scheme with no additional onsite parking, by reason of absence of parking survey to demonstrate there is capacity in the locality to accommodate the parking shortfall, the scheme would adversely impact on parking, the free flow of traffic and pedestrian and vehicular safety on the surrounding roads.  The scheme fails to comply with, in particular, Policy T6 of the London Plan and Policy T16.1 of Merton's Local Plan 2024.

Reason : 5 - In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory cycle parking provision, the development has failed to provide sufficient secure, integrated, convenient and accessible cycle parking facilities and thus fail to promote sustainable form of transport, contrary to, in particular, policy T16.2 of  Merton�s Local Plan 2024 and T5 of the London Plan 2021.

Reason : 6 - In the absence of adequate refuse and recycling storage facilities for the development, the applicant has not demonstrated that the scheme would not adversely impact on the free flow of traffic in the locality to the detriment of highway and pedestrian safety and result in material harm to the visual amenity  of the area.  The scheme is contrary to, in particular, Policies D4, SI 7 & SI 8 of the London Plan 2021,  Merton Local Plan 2024 policy D12.2, D12.3 and W14.4.

Reason : 7 - By reason of the lack of an energy statement (demonstrating that the scheme would achieve a 100% improvement on Part L, Building regulations 2021), a lack of information to demonstrate water usage rates and a lack of information relating to ventilation or overheating, the applicant has failed to demonstrate that the application would meet the requirement of Policies CC2.1, CC2.2, CC2.3, CC2.4 CC2.5and CC2.6.
Reason : 8 - The applicant has failed to provide a soft-landscaping scheme, thereby failing to comply the objectives set out in G5 of the London Plan 2021.

Reason : 9 - In the absence of a Biodiversity Net Gain Statement incorporating aerial images of the site, marked up to show existing development areas, and how that accords with the exemption criteria claimed, together with photographs of the current site conditions, the scheme fails to comply with requirements set out in, in particular, the Environment Act 2021, The Biodiversity Gain Requirements (Exemptions) Regulations 2024 and Merton Local Plan Policy O15.3.

Reason : 10 - In the absence of a Flood Risk Assessment incorporating Sustainable Urban Drainage Design, it has not been demonstrated the scheme would safeguard the risk of flooding in the locality.  The proposal is contrary to, in particular, London Plan policy SI 13 and Merton Local Plan policies 15.7 & 15.8

Reason : 11 - In the absence of a s106 legal agreement securing the required financial contribution towards affordable housing or a financial viability assessment to justify the lack of, the scheme fails to comply with, in particular, policy H11.1 of Merton Local Plan (2024).

Reason : 12 - In the absence of a satisfactory Air Quality Neutral Statement, the applicant has failed to demonstrate that the development would be at minimum air quality neutral, not worsening local air quality thereby failing to comply with policy SI1 of the London Plan 2021

Reason : 13 - In the absence of a fire safety strategy, the applicant has failed to demonstrate that the development would provide the highest standard of fire safety, thereby failing to comply with policy D12 of the London Plan 2021.

Reason : 14 - INFORMATIVE
Note to Applicant
In accordance with paragraph 38 of the NPPF, The London Borough of Merton  (LBM) takes a positive and proactive approach to development proposals focused on solutions. LBM works with applicants/agents in a positive and proactive manner by:
"	Offering a pre-application advice and duty desk service. 
"	Where possible, suggesting solutions to secure a successful outcome.
"	As appropriate, updating applicants/agents of any issues that may arise in the processing of their application.
In this instance:
"	The application was not considered to comply with the provisions of the Development Plan and NPPF as submitted, and would have required substantial changes such that a new application would be required. 
"	It is noted that the applicant/agent did not engage in any pre-application discussions.
"	The applicant is advised to seek pre-application advice on any resubmission.
